html:
The Arusha Accords for Burundi were signed on 28 August 2000 at Arusha in Tanzania, setting out a peace and power sharing plan to end the Burundian Civil War.

Talks begun under Julius Nyerere were finished by Nelson Mandela after Nyerere died in 1999. The deal gave Hutu 60 percent and Tutsi 40 percent of posts in government and parliament, split the army equally, and limited presidents to two terms.

The main rebel groups did not sign at first and fought on for some years. The quotas eased the old fear of Tutsi domination and Hutu revenge. The limit on terms was at the heart of the crisis of 2015.
sum: The Arusha Accords for Burundi were signed on 28 August 2000 at Arusha in Tanzania, setting out a peace and power sharing plan to end the Burundian Civil War.
